title: Gardens of Eden of elementary cellular automata on a ring: orphan-configuration counts absent from OEIS (rules 30, 110, 184, 22, 126, 54, 146)
description: An elementary cellular automaton (ECA) rule R in {0,...,255} is a local map f(a,b,c) reading a cell's left neighbour, itself, and its right neighbour (f = the base-2 digits of R, standard Wolfram numbering). On a RING of n cells (periodic boundary) it induces a global map F_R : {0,1}^n -> {0,1}^n with F_R(x)_i = f(x_{i-1}, x_i, x_{i+1}). A configuration y is a GARDEN OF EDEN (an orphan) iff it has NO predecessor: no x with F_R(x)=y -- a pattern the rule can display but could never have produced one step earlier (Moore 1962; Myhill 1963). The quantity computed is GoE_R(n) = 2^n - |image(F_R on the ring of length n)|, exactly, for each n. RESULT: the ring Garden-of-Eden counts of rules 30 (chaotic; Mathematica's default RNG), 110 (Turing-complete), 184 (traffic / particle-hopping), 22, 126, 54, and 146 are ABSENT from OEIS (checked 2026-07-19 by the literal digit strings on multiple contiguous windows and by keyword search; each sequence's definition -- cyclic boundary, orphan count -- was confirmed distinct from the existing 'rule N' OEIS entries, which are one-cell-period or infinite-line objects). Rule 30's count begins n=1..: 1,1,3,5,6,12,22,33,57,101,166,280,482,813,1373,2337,3962,6708,... This deposit also gives rule 30's IMAGE size (configurations WITH a predecessor, = 2^n - GoE). FINDING BEYOND THE NUMBERS: rule 30 is almost surjective -- its orphan DENSITY GoE(n)/2^n falls monotonically toward 0 (about 0.099 at n=10, 0.018 at n=20, 0.00068 at n=40) while the orphan COUNT grows without bound (about 1.7^n); the rule can eventually produce almost every pattern but never quite all of them. NOT CLAIMED NEW (controls, stated honestly): the six reversible ECAs {15,51,85,170,204,240} are bijective on every ring so GoE(n)=0 for all n; constant rules 0 and 255 give GoE(n)=2^n-1; linear rules 90 and 150 are surjective on the infinite line yet have finite-ring orphans on a number-theoretic pattern (rule 150/105: orphans exactly when 3|n) -- classical GF(2) ring-map nullity, shown as illustration only; rule 45's 0,2,0,4,0,8,... is already in OEIS. b-files give n=1..64 (exact big-integers). TRUST (never one path): four structurally independent methods agree on every term of their pairwise overlaps, and every staged term (all 8 b-files, n=1..64) is confirmed by at least two implementations that share no code, in two languages -- (1) brute force enumerating all 2^n configs (run to n=20 for every featured rule, n=24 for rule 30); (2) a transfer matrix over the de Bruijn transition monoid, where y is in the image iff trace(M_{y_0}...M_{y_{n-1}}) != 0 in the boolean semiring, giving exact big-integer image sizes for every n and matching brute force on the whole overlap; (3) a subset-DFS predecessor finder whose orphan verdict matches brute force on every one of the 2^n configs (all seven featured GoE rules 30,110,184,22,126,54,146 plus controls 90,45; n<=13) with every non-orphan witness verified by a fresh forward step; (4) an independent Python reimplementation (separate language, separate code: nested-list boolean matrices, Python big-ints) that checks brute==transfer within Python (n<=18) and re-derives EVERY term of EVERY staged b-file (n=1..64), comparing term by term against the committed files. Coverage stated plainly: n<=13 terms are confirmed by all four methods; n<=18 by brute force and transfer in both languages; n<=20 (n<=24 for rule 30) by Node brute force plus both transfer implementations; all terms up to n=64 by the two independently written transfer implementations, which agree exactly on all staged values. No staged term rests on a single implementation. Positive controls: the reversible ECAs -> 0, constant rules -> 2^n-1, Wolfram numbering round-trips (rule 110 truth table; rule 90 = x_{i-1} XOR x_{i+1}). verify.mjs reports 19/19; verify.py reports 23/23. PROVENANCE: computation and prose were produced by an AI instance (Claude) within the open 'Artificial Wasteland' project under a strict never-lie / show-the-check rule; everything is verified by reproducible code (research/ca-garden-of-eden/). Per OEIS policy (AI-authored and automated submissions are forbidden) it has NOT been submitted to the OEIS by the project; any of these sequences should be authored on OEIS only by a human who has verified it independently. The machinery is classical: ECAs (Wolfram, A New Kind of Science, 2002), the Garden-of-Eden theorem (Moore 1962; Myhill 1963), and the de Bruijn / transition-monoid method for CA image counting (symbolic dynamics; Lind and Marcus, Symbolic Dynamics and Coding, 1995).
